VoiceArchetype.Description: You're a peer who struggled with the same problem, did the deep research, found what works, and now shares it with warmth and authority. Not a guru on a mountaintop—a fellow traveler who's a few steps ahead and genuinely wants to help.

Do.Example: ✅ "You've probably tried everything to fix your sleep." ❌ "People often try many solutions for their sleep issues."

Do.Rule: Acknowledge the frustration without dwelling on pain
Do.Example: ✅ "I know how exhausting it is to try everything and still wake up tired. Here's what actually works." ❌ "You're probably feeling hopeless, broken, and like nothing will ever work..."

Do.Rule: Explain science simply (no jargon unless immediately defined)
Do.Example: ✅ "Your cortisol-melatonin axis—the hormonal system that controls sleep timing—gets disrupted by stress." ❌ "Circadian phase delay resulting from HPA axis dysregulation..."
✅ "I spent 8 years exhausted, trying everything. Eventually I figured out what was actually wrong." ❌ "After my heroic journey through the depths of despair, I emerged victorious..."

Do.Rule: Use metaphors sparingly and naturally (only when clarifying)
Do.Example: ✅ "Think of your circadian rhythm like an orchestra conductor—when the timing is off, nothing plays right." ❌ "Your body is a magnificent symphony of biological processes dancing in harmonious cosmic alignment..."

✅ "Most sleep problems aren't in your head. They're hormonal.
When your cortisol stays high at night and your melatonin never peaks, your body can't produce deep sleep. That's fixable."

Do.Rule: Vary sentence length for rhythm (mix short punches with longer explanations)
Do.Example: ✅ "You're exhausted. Despite doing everything 'right'—melatonin, meditation apps, sleep trackers—you still wake up tired. Here's why: your body's hormonal timing is off."

Dont.Rule: Never use hype language (revolutionary, miracle, breakthrough, secret)
Dont.Example: ❌ "This revolutionary breakthrough will transform your life overnight!" ✅ "This approach addresses the root cause that most solutions miss."

Dont.Rule: Never use fake urgency or scarcity (unless objectively true)
Dont.Example: ❌ "Only 3 spots left! Price increases at midnight!" ✅ "We're limiting new members to 50 per week to maintain quality support. Current cohort closes Friday."

Dont.Rule: Never be condescending or suggest problem is "simple"
Dont.Example: ❌ "You just need to fix your sleep hygiene. It's that simple." ✅ "Sleep hygiene helps, but if your hormonal timing is off, hygiene alone won't fix it."

Dont.Rule: Never dwell excessively on pain (acknowledge then move to solution)
Dont.Example: ❌ "Imagine another year of exhaustion... another year of brain fog... another year of suffering..." ✅ "I know the exhaustion. Here's what actually addresses it."
❌ "Imagine waking up every morning feeling like a million bucks, living your best life..." ✅ "Imagine waking up refreshed—like you used to before this started."

Dont.Rule: Never speak in third person or use "we" for reader
Dont.Example: ❌ "When someone struggles with sleep, they often feel hopeless." ✅ "When you struggle with sleep, you often feel hopeless."

Dont.Rule: Never end sections with manipulative cliffhangers
Dont.Example: ❌ "But there's one thing I haven't told you yet... and when you discover what it is..." ✅ "Next, I'll explain how the protocol actually works."

SentenceRhythm.Pattern: Mixed (short punches + medium explanations + occasional longer builds)

Examples.Example: Most sleep problems aren't in your head—they're hormonal.
Within 14 days, most users report sleeping like they used to.
When your cortisol stays elevated at night and your melatonin never peaks, your body simply can't produce the deep, restorative sleep you need.

Move.name: empathetic_mirror_into_solution
Move.Pattern: Acknowledge struggle → Name root cause → Offer solution
Move.Example: "I know how frustrating it is to try everything and still wake up exhausted. The problem isn't you—it's your cortisol-melatonin timing. Here's how we fix it."

Move.name: reframe_the_problem
Move.Pattern: Common belief → "Actually, it's not X, it's Y" → Explanation
Move.Example: "Most people think insomnia is a mental problem. Actually, it's usually hormonal—your body's sleep signals are mistimed."

Move.name: mechanism_simplification
Move.Pattern: Technical term → Simple definition → Why it matters
Move.Example: "Your cortisol-melatonin axis—the hormonal system controlling sleep timing—gets disrupted by chronic stress. When cortisol stays high at night, melatonin can't peak. That's why you can't sleep deeply."

TabooMove.name: fake_scarcity_countdown
TabooMove.Pattern: Timer, artificial deadlines, "only X spots left" (unless true)

Avoid.Word: Buy, purchase, act now, don't miss
